tion": "How does haythu ma kuntum work grammatically?", "turns_on": "Whether ma makes haythu conditional and how the verb and response are construed.", "positions": [{"id": "2:144/q24/p1", "position": "Haythu ma forms a locative condition, answered by fa-wallū.", "reasons": "TAB-FULL: Haythu ma forms a locative condition, answered by fa-wallū. SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (author): On the conditional analysis, kuntum is jussive, wallū answers the condition, and ḥaythumā is an accusative adverb governed by kuntum; Q 17:110 illustrates the construction. | mentions 17:110 SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (الشيخ): Although ḥayth is a locative noun normally annexed to a clause in the genitive, its connection with mā removes annexation and gives it conditional force and verbal governance.
